original_value: The functionality of three dry electrocardiogram electrode constructions was evaluated by measuring canine heart rate during four different behaviors: Standing, sitting, lying and walking. The testing was repeated (n = 9) in each of the 36 scenarios with three dogs. Two of the electrodes were constructed with spring-loaded test pins while the third electrode was a molded polymer electrode with Ag/AgCl coating. During the measurement, a specifically designed harness was used to attach the electrodes to the dogs. The performance of the electrodes was evaluated and compared in terms of heartbeat detection coverage. The effect on the respective heart rate coverage was studied by computing the heart rate coverage from the measured electrocardiogram signal using a pattern-matching algorithm to extract the R-peaks and further the beat-to-beat heart rate. The results show that the overall coverage ratios regarding the electrodes varied between 45–95% in four different activity modes. The lowest coverage was for lying and walking and the highest was for standing and sitting.

result.paraphrase: The performance of three dry electrocardiogram electrode designs was assessed by measuring canine heart rate across four behaviors: standing, sitting, lying, and walking. Tests were repeated nine times (n = 9) for each of the 36 scenarios involving three dogs. Two electrodes used spring-loaded test pins, while the third was a molded polymer electrode with an Ag/AgCl coating. A specially designed harness attached the electrodes to the dogs during measurement. Electrode performance was evaluated and compared by heartbeat detection coverage, with heart rate coverage computed from the recorded ECG signal using a pattern-matching algorithm to identify R-peaks and derive beat-to-beat heart rate. The results showed overall coverage ratios of 45–95% across the four activity modes, with the lowest coverage during lying and walking and the highest during standing and sitting.
